module.title: PM in BigTech: Skill Test
module.subtitle: 20+ EXERCISES / 45 MINS OF PRACTICE
module.description: About 20 tasks, built according to the logic of the product life cycle. Working with metrics, prioritization, planning, customer interviews, Mixpanel reports, SQL, API calls, and unit economics.

lesson.title: Find Your PM Blind Spots
lesson.note: Blocks are ordered. type=message/artifact/tool/question/continue/feedback. Options carry weight (1 full, 0.5 partial, 0 wrong) and a feedbackId. Highlight keywords with **bold** or a highlight span in rendering. This seed reproduces the first 5 verified tasks; later tasks (API, unit economics, A/B, interviews, LLM) follow the same shell and should be authored similarly.

blocks.markdown: Hello! I'm here to guide you through this simulator. The PM profession requires several skills at once: OKRs, SQL, analytics, user interviews, API testing, A/B testing, unit economics, and LLMs. We've prepared 20+ practice tasks. You'll work with real tools like SQL, Mixpanel, APIs, and Replit AI. ~30 min. A 10% coupon awaits at the end.
Hi! I'm your senior colleague. Our product is a clothing rental service by subscription. We have quarterly planning today and haven't defined OKRs yet. What do you think of this Q2 draft?

blocks.content:
Objective: Reach self-sufficiency by the end of the quarter

Key Results:
- Increase the conversion rate of the main landing page
- Increase the percentage of successful payments
- Add new clothing categories

options.label: I'm not quite sure what this is about....
Tasks must be related to each other

blocks.markdown: It's okay to not have numbers in the Objective — it should be descriptive, ambitious, motivating. But KRs must be clear and measurable. Big difference between 'increase conversion' and 'increase conversion by 20%'. Let's improve this OKR.
How do you like this version?

blocks.content:
Objective: Reach self-sufficiency by the end of the quarter

Key Results:
- Increase the conversion rate of the main landing page from 4% to 7%
- Increase the percentage of successful payments from 80% to 90% by adding an automatic testing mechanism
- Add 4 new clothing categories
- Continue to fix emerging bugs

blocks.markdown: Better — fixed immeasurability, but added two problems: 'continue to fix bugs' is a process not a result; 'by adding a mechanism...' prescribes HOW (the team decides how).
Taking all that into account, the Q2 OKR looks like this:

blocks.content:
Objective: Reach self-sufficiency by the end of the quarter

Key Results:
- Increase the conversion rate of the main landing page from 4% to 7%
- Increase the percentage of successful payments from 80% to 90%
- Bring in +7% new users

options.label: Well, now it's a definite yes.

blocks.markdown: Professional OKR. Note the last line changed from a HOW (4 categories) to a RESULT (+7% new traffic). OKR = ambitious Objective + specific, measurable, achievable KRs that don't dictate how. PM owns 3 horizons: short-term (sprint user stories), medium (OKRs/epics), long (strategy/vision/mission).
Our marketer was looking for you — she's having trouble with her metrics and was in a panic. Please help her.

Hi! I have a quarterly report and my manager said 'Can't you write simple SQL?' I need to know how many January paid subscriptions came from **Google Ads**. My query only shows all subscriptions for the period. Can you count only the Google ones?

blocks.content:
SELECT COUNT(user_id) --"Select the number of user IDs"
FROM viditation_user -- "from the viditation_user table"
WHERE is_premium = TRUE --"who paid for the premium subscription"
AND created_date between '2022-01-01' and '2022-02-01' --"purchase date Jan 1 – Feb 1"

blocks.collapsedLabel: If you want to run the query yourself

blocks.prompt: Count only users who came from Google.

options.label: I'm too lazy to run the query, but I know I need to add "AND acquisition_channel = 'google'" as the last line.
I'm too lazy to run the query, but I know I need to add "IN CASE acquisition_channel = 'google'" as the last line.

blocks.markdown: Wow, 17 subscriptions — so we won't develop this channel. You just add `AND acquisition_channel = 'google'` as the last line. ('IN CASE' is not valid SQL.)
I need to calculate MAU (Monthly Active Users) for January. All I have is average WAU by week for January, and it's 180. Please calculate MAU for January.

options.label: It is clear that it is impossible to determine MAU here

blocks.markdown: Indeed! Audience for a period = unique users who visited at least once. Knowing only avg weekly uniques (180), MAU could be anywhere from 180 (same people every week) to ~720 (WAU*4, different people). Without the visit-distribution we can't know — a 4x difference is too big to guess.

blocks.label: We need to look at the analytical data!

blocks.markdown: You PMs use Mixpanel. Behavioral analytics stores 'everything' (visits, clicks, feature use), so you can quickly test ideas. I made a chart by week for January — see the screenshot. What is MAU for January?

blocks.collapsedLabel: If you want to play with the report yourself

options.label: I opened the report in Mixpanel, and I see 1083 per month
I opened the report in Mixpanel, and I see 579 per month
I opened the report in Mixpanel, and I see 872 per month
I'm too lazy to open Mixpanel, but you can use the screenshot: the sum of the weekly values is 1083
I'm too lazy to open Mixpanel, but you can't determine MAU from a screenshot alone

blocks.markdown: Exactly! You can't sum weekly uniques — weekly-unique visitors aren't necessarily unique for the month (some visit twice). Switch the report to monthly grouping and Mixpanel computes it: MAU = 579. Not at all what the simpler methods assumed.

Last one! We're improving a 5-step onboarding. Overall conversion is only ~35% (2,074 finished / 5,952 started). We can only fix one step for the biggest impact. Column labels show % who reached this step from the previous (top) and absolute count (bottom). Which step should we improve first?

blocks.collapsedLabel: here is a link to this chart in Mixpanel

blocks.markdown: Absolutely right! The largest drop is after Step 1 — only 62.57% move from Step 1 to Step 2. That's where a fix has the biggest impact on overall conversion. Prioritize the biggest drop-off, not the overall rate.
